facts.text: The user provided advice from the book "Golden Grant Rules" by David Kincade.
The user discussed improving writing for grant applications.
The user said grant agencies read a dozen or so applications and move clearly written applications to a "next" pile for further consideration.
The user said grant applications need impressive technology and clear writing to be winnable.
The user said to speak to the grant agency to confirm they love the innovation before focusing on writing quality.
The user said the most common writing mistake is sentences that span two or three lines.
The user said longer type sentences can be used, but short sentences should also be used to give the reader a rest.
The user said a longer sentence followed by a shorter one helps the reader.
The user said grant agencies have helped people they know who are terrible at writing with their applications.
The user said learning to write in the active voice helps all writing, not just grants.
The user cited Purdue University's writing center definition that active voice makes meaning clear and keeps sentences from becoming too complicated or wordy.
The user said to use the difference between dependent and independent clauses in nearly every email or document.
The user cited Purdue University's writing center definition that an independent clause expresses a complete thought and is a sentence, while a dependent clause cannot be a sentence.
The user said when the independent clause is before the dependent clause, you do not use a comma.
The user said investing 15 minutes of life in learning dependent vs. independent clauses is worth it.
The user said when starting a sentence with the word "This," you should put a subject after it.
The user said the word "it" can lose the reader if the reader cannot easily discern what "it" refers to.
The user gave an example of replacing "it" with "deliveries" or "the drone" to make a sentence stronger.
The user said grant reality is accuracy over brilliance.
The user said the grant agency's job is to ensure the application meets funding criteria, not determine how successful the product will be.
The user said if the best idea is not filled out correctly, the applicant will most likely lose.
The user said if the applicant makes the grant agency's life easy, the application will stand out.
The user said the secret sauce to winning grants is impact.
The user said the government needs to invest in the project by significantly impacting many taxpayers' well-being.
The user said impact can include massive job creation, GHG emission reductions, significant potential tax revenue, export potential, or survivability.
The user said to measure impact by looking at the grant agency's mandate and aligning the project's impact with it.
The user said the project "needs to be cool" according to a high-level grant agency staffer.
The user said a grant agency staffer at a recent conference said the grant application should hit all the points the grant agency is looking for.
The user said the grant application should be written to help the grant agency achieve its mandate, not to enhance the user's mandate.
The user said most people do not want to write grant applications, so they consider hiring a grant writer.
The user said hiring a grant writer increases the chance of actually getting the grant submitted.
The user said starting and stopping a detailed grant application slows the process dramatically.
The user said the learning curve for grant writing can be dreadful.
The user said grant writing is challenging and requires being organized, getting along with people, writing clearly, and having incredible attention to detail.
The user said finding someone with those skill sets is rare.
The user said if the user found such a person, they should hang on to that person.
The user said a grant trap occurred when a man emailed with a question about grants and the grant maximum was $25,000 while his total budget came in just over.
The user said the man's application was automatically rejected because of that error.

The user said hiring a grant writer requires one-on-one time because the entrepreneur may have go-to-market strategy, intellectual property situation, competition, export plan, and team biography information in their head.
The user said delegating everything to the grant writer, especially on the first draft, is more likely a collaboration than a delegation.
The user said a secret is that grant agency staff hate grant writers.
The user said when meeting the grant agency, the owner or president should be brought to the first meeting.
The user said not to send the grant writer alone to the first meeting with the grant agency.
The user said as a rule of thumb, if a grant will take 40 hours to complete, the entrepreneur needs to contribute at least eight of those hours.
The user said the entrepreneur cannot delegate the entire process, especially the first grant application.
The user said the 100% commission model for grant writers is not possible because grants have eligible expenses and the grant writer needs to be paid from the company's bank account.
The user said if the organization has no money, then a 100% commission arrangement cannot work.

The user said when a grant writer starts working with a company, the business obviously loves the technology, but it is unknown whether the grant agency loves it or has already funded a similar project.
The user said many variables are outside of the grant writer's control.
The user said grant writers must be smart and ensure the contract does not wholly rely on the business winning the grant.
The user said the grant writer's job is to write a clear proposal (no application yet) to the grant agency for a "heck yes" or "no."
The user said the grant writer needs money upfront to cover costs.
The user said paying someone 100% commission can be a major problem because they may not be around to finish the job.
The user said it can take on average 4-8 weeks to write the grant after engaging a grant writer.
The user said the government can take 6-12 weeks (or way more) to determine if you win.
The user said grants are reimbursed after spending money, and reimbursement can take a minimum of three months and more likely 4-6 months.
The user said an independent grant writer could go one day to months without payment and it could be a year.
The user said the user found that businesses hire grant writers on commission and the grant writer does not stick around long enough to submit the grant.
The user said paying a small amount upfront with an incentive, if successful, can be a long-term solution for both parties.
The user said to find a proven grant writer with references and that if there is a "heck ya" from the grant agency, the applicant should apply.
The user referenced another rule called "The rules and regulations of grant commissions" for more about incentives and commissions.

events.text: Grant application writing advice about what happens at the judging stage (read a dozen or so; move to the "next" pile).
A recent conference where a grant agency staffer said the application should hit all the points the grant agency is looking for.
A grant trap example where a man’s application was automatically rejected because the grant maximum was $25,000 and his total budget came in just over.
A first meeting with the grant agency where the owner or president should attend and the grant writer should not go alone.
A timeline example for grant writing and approval: 4-8 weeks to write, 6-12 weeks (or more) for government decision, and 3+ months (more likely 4-6 months) for reimbursement.
